item.title: Single Dose of Frog-Derived Gut Bacterium Eradicates 100% of Tumors in Mice
item.description:
📝 NEW STUDY: Frog-Derived Gut Bacterium Completely Eradicates 100% of Tumors After a Single Dose in MiceA single intravenous dose of Ewingella americana achieved complete tumor elimination in 100% of treated animals, with no detectable toxicity—outperforming chemotherapy and immunotherapy. Investigators observed approximately a 3,000-fold increase in bacterial load within tumors within 24 hours, indicating highly efficient tumor homing and intratumoral expansion. The organism was rapidly cleared from circulation within 24 hours, while remaining selectively localized within tumor tissue—an unusual and highly favorable pharmacokinetic pattern.
🔗 Read more: https://www.thefocalpoints.com/p/new-study-frog-derived-gut-bacterium

item.title: Launch HN: Parsewise (YC P25) – Reason Across Documents with an API
item.description:
📝 Hi all, it’s Greg and Max, founders of Parsewise hereParsewise transforms a bucket of unstructured data into schema compliant data retaining lineage for values resolved across documents. I am NOT looking for something that would just extract data point by data point, page by page into a structured well-defined schema but more something more agentic that can understand that information might be across documents and that it should reason over what to extract. At the core of the data processing we have self-improving agent definitions.
🔗 Read more: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48746752

item.title: Your Kids' School Bus Is About to Become a Roaming Surveillance Vehicle
item.description:
📝 The report is based on leaked documents from BusPatrol, a company that specializes in stop-arm cameras that capture images of drivers illegally passing school buses (“stop-arm” is the proper name of the fold-out stop signs on school buses). And according to the report, BusPatrol now wants to turn those cameras into license plate readers. If BusPatrol goes ahead with this plan, these cameras would join an already-dense surveillance net that can track people’s movements by reading license plates or the signals from electronic devices.
🔗 Read more: https://www.thedrive.com/news/your-kids-school-bus-is-about-to-become-a-roaming-surveillance-vehicle

item.title: Pine64 launch $50 smart speaker for Home Assistant tinkerers
item.description:
📝 Open-hardware manufacturer Pine64 has launched a $50 smart speaker that runs open-source software on a RISC-V chip. PineVoice isn’t an all-singing smart speaker PineVoice isn’t a rival to Echoes, Nests or HomePods PineVoice is in an early-stage development and early adopters will encounter quirks and performance issues. Unlike those proprietary consumer devices, which rely on cloud ecosystems, PineVoice is built for local, open-source networks.
🔗 Read more: https://www.omgubuntu.co.uk/2026/06/pine64-pinevoice-riscv-smart-speaker-launch
